title: Write the Trace and Provenance sweep procedures in one home and cite them
action:
Create skills/bee-researching/references/trace-and-provenance.md as the SINGLE HOME for two named procedures, then point two existing surfaces at it. Per pstack-gaps D1, D2, D3.

File shape: a one-line H1, then exactly two H2 sections, `## Trace` and `## Provenance sweep`. Match the house voice of skills/bee-researching/references/research-protocol.md — numbered steps, short imperative sentences, no code blocks, no tables unless a table is the clearest shape. Keep the whole file under 90 lines.

`## Trace` answers 'how does this actually run?'. It MUST state, per D2: (a) the outcome is a runtime path with path:line anchors, never a file list; (b) the leader picks 2 to 4 DISJOINT entry points and fans one read-only worker at each through the dispatch door — the exact door is `.bee/bin/bee dispatch prepare --runtime <rt> --kind gather --json`, run first, then the tool and payload it returns; never a hand-picked subagent_type or model; (c) four is a ceiling and two is a floor, and a trace with only ONE honest entry point runs INLINE and says so in the account; (d) the leader folds every return into ONE account — the workers' returns are never pasted; (e) a step the trace could not follow is named as unfollowed, with the reason.

`## Provenance sweep` answers 'why is this the way it is?'. It MUST list exactly the SEVEN evidence categories from D3, in this order, each with the concrete command or path that sweeps it in this repo: 1. decision log (`bee decisions search --text`), 2. git history (`git log -S`, `git log --follow`), 3. `docs/history/<feature>/` (CONTEXT.md, plan.md, reports/), 4. the knowledge bundle (`bee knowledge search --text`, docs/knowledge/), 5. code comments and doc-comments in the owning source file, 6. tests that name the behavior, 7. the external tracker (issues and PRs), which is often absent — say so rather than skipping it. It MUST state that every category returning NOTHING is reported BY NAME as empty, and a category not swept at all is reported as unswept — an omitted category is the defect the procedure exists to stop.

Then the two citations, and nothing more:
- skills/bee-researching/SKILL.md: add ONE row to the `## References` table, in the existing row shape, naming `references/trace-and-provenance.md` and when to load it (a how-does-this-run question, or a why-is-this-so question).
- skills/bee-planning/references/planning-reference.md: in the `### research` playbook under `## Class playbooks`, add ONE pointer line after the numbered steps naming this new file and its two section names. Do NOT transcribe the steps and do NOT renumber or reword the existing four steps.

Do not touch any other file. Do not add a route class, a lane, a skill, or a guard.

REGEN, inside this cell and in this order: `.bee/bin/bee dev render-skill-trees`, then `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --apply`, then `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --write`. Commit the regenerated copies with the change; a hand-edited generated copy is a defect.
verify: skills/bee-researching/references/trace-and-provenance.md exists with exactly the two H2 sections `## Trace` and `## Provenance sweep`; the Trace section names the 2-to-4 ceiling and the `bee dispatch prepare` door; the Provenance sweep section lists seven numbered categories and states the empty-by-name rule. `rg -n 'trace-and-provenance' skills/` returns a row in bee-researching/SKILL.md's References table AND a pointer line in bee-planning/references/planning-reference.md. `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` runs clean. `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check` is clean.
